title: Isolate project hooks in Cursor review workspace
description:
## Problem

The comprehensive-review Cursor adapter now uses --trust --workspace <repository> to avoid non-interactive workspace-trust startup failures. Cursor project hooks can execute scripts in trusted workspaces. Ask mode and --sandbox enabled constrain agent tools but do not establish isolation for hook execution. The installed CLI hook executor uses an unsandboxed policy and can load both .cursor/hooks.json and hooks from .claude settings.

Affected code: plugins/jig-review/skills/comprehensive-review/scripts/cursor-review.mjs, buildCursorArgs; associated SKILL.md and references/parallel-review-runtime.md.

## Accepted trade-off

The user explicitly accepted this trade-off for now and requested that it be tracked for future work. Keep the current --trust behavior, ask mode, and sandboxing. This is deferred hardening, not a blocker for the current fix. No implementation work is requested now.

## Future approach

Check for a supported CLI control to disable project hooks. None was found in the inspected CLI help/documentation. --skip-worktree-setup only skips worktree setup scripts.

If no suitable control exists, run Cursor against a temporary source snapshot without active project hook/configuration files, including .cursor and .claude configuration. Preserve changes to excluded files as inert review evidence. Trust only the temporary workspace; do not add the original repository as another workspace root. Preserve source locations, scope-fingerprint verification, coverage disclosures, and cleanup on success, failure, timeout, and cancellation. A plain Git worktree retains tracked hook configuration and is insufficient by itself.

A smaller alternative is a temporary workspace containing only the bounded review assignment, with reduced surrounding-source inspection disclosed. Project isolation does not disable user or enterprise hooks; constraining all hooks requires isolation around the entire Cursor process.

## Validation and open questions

- Establish whether project hooks execute under the exact --print --mode ask --sandbox enabled --trust invocation; this was not reproduced during review.
- Determine whether --trust persists after process exit.
- Use a harmless sentinel hook in a fresh, previously untrusted fixture to verify the eventual solution prevents project-hook execution while the review still completes.
- Verify changed hook configuration remains reviewable as inert evidence and findings map to original repository paths.
- Disclose Cursor workspace trust in final review notes.

Evidence: https://prod.cursor.com/docs/hooks and https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/parameters. The existing adapter tests use a fake Cursor executable and do not prove real CLI hook isolation.

title: Preserve patch coverage for large external-review diffs
description:
## Reported behavior

A comprehensive review reported Codex completed, Claude completed with limited coverage because its supplied diff was truncated, Claude file access restricted, and scope fingerprint verified unchanged. Cursor separately failed on workspace trust; that startup issue is handled by the current --trust change, with future hook isolation tracked in jig-skills-h18.

## Source-backed cause

plugins/jig-review/skills/comprehensive-review/scripts/review-context.mjs sets MAX_DIFF_BYTES to 384 KiB per diff capture and MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES to 768 KiB for assembled context sections. boundedDiff replaces an oversized full patch with git --stat and an omission notice; ContextBuilder.add can also truncate/drop later sections at the aggregate limit. The reported notes do not identify which limit was hit in that particular run.

The fallback asks the reviewer to inspect current files. Claude exposes only Read, Glob, and Grep and prohibits shell commands, so reading current files cannot generally reconstruct omitted base/index versions, deletions, or staged versus unstaged changes. Restricted mode is not the source of the adapter byte caps; switching to host access would not solve this.

Both Claude and Cursor use this shared context collector, so the limit is not Claude-specific. A verified scope fingerprint proves scope stability, not full review coverage. Existing incomplete-coverage disclosure is correct and must remain.

## Proposed follow-up

Provide a bounded way to retrieve complete patches incrementally: for example, per-file/hunk evidence chunks with a manifest, accessible to each reviewer through read-only tools. Preserve base/index/current distinctions, deletions, untracked files, initialized submodule changes, and original source locations. For Claude restricted access, design evidence access without requiring a broad host-access opt-out or altering the fingerprinted scope.

Retain overall deadlines, bounded memory, isolation between reviewers, and explicit omission/coverage accounting. Simply increasing limits postpones the failure and risks exceeding model context capacity. Do not claim complete coverage merely because all chunks were made available; track what was reviewed and disclose anything omitted.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reproduce the 384 KiB single-diff fallback and 768 KiB aggregate truncation independently with deterministic fixtures.
- Make changes beyond both thresholds available as actual before/after patch evidence, including a deletion and staged/unstaged versions that current-file reads cannot reconstruct.
- Verify read-only evidence access works for Claude restricted mode and the Cursor adapter without weakening tool permissions or scope checks.
- Preserve partial-coverage reporting for genuine resource/deadline limits, separately from fingerprint status.
- Include an integration check of evidence access with the real CLI when implementing the solution; mocked argument checks alone do not prove coverage.

Tracked for future work; no adapter behavior changed as part of recording this issue.
